gen_risks.description: ADISA and the new PMU have very weak procurement capacity, risking non‑compliant purchases and delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit experienced procurement staff, provide Bank‑led training, use sample TORs, and maintain close Bank oversight during early procurement cycles.
gen_risks.evidence: Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA as a newly created agency. (Procurement risk rating section)

gen_risks.description: Failure to achieve DLI#5 (policy reform document and baseline survey) will block all RBF disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize DLI#5 early, allocate PPF funds for the baseline survey, set a strict timeline, and monitor progress weekly.
gen_risks.evidence: No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved. (Disbursement conditions)

gen_risks.description: Complex inter‑ministerial coordination may cause delays or inconsistent implementation of reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen the Steering Committee, hold regular joint meetings, define clear TORs for Working Groups, and use the DU as a coordination hub.
gen_risks.evidence: Complex coordination... multiple lead agencies... risk of bureaucratic resistance. (Coordination section)

gen_risks.description: Seven key agencies lack any IT system, hindering backend automation and service digitisation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fast‑track IT development with TA support, adopt a phased rollout, and ensure NAIS provides integration assistance.
gen_risks.evidence: Seven institutions encompassed by the proposed project have no IT system in place. (Component 1 description)

gen_risks.description: Low internet penetration may exclude poor and vulnerable groups from e‑services, undermining equity goals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain physical CSCs, create assisted access points (internet cafés, community centres), and run targeted outreach campaigns.
gen_risks.evidence: Risk that focus on state‑of‑the‑art means could diminish access of the poor and vulnerable. (Section 6)

gen_risks.description: Construction of the central CSC could generate dust, noise, waste and traffic impacts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Environmental Management Plan, enforce construction best practices, obtain required permits, and monitor impacts continuously.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential environmental impacts... dust and noise, waste generation... mitigated through EMP. (Environment section)

gen_risks.description: Entrenched corruption and staff resistance may impede reform of front‑office processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy a change‑management program, provide ethics training, link performance incentives to citizen‑feedback results, and monitor via the feedback mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: Corruption remains high... risk of resistance to reforms. (Corruption survey section)

gen_risks.description: Overall financial management risk is substantial due to ADISA’s limited fiduciary experience.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire two qualified finance specialists, adopt a detailed Financial Management Manual, and conduct regular Bank‑led training and audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial... ADISA has limited experience. (Financial Management section)

gen_risks.description: Unfilled procurement and administrative specialist positions delay procurement planning and execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate recruitment, use interim staff or consultants, and leverage Bank procurement experts for early guidance.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement and Administrative Specialist positions have been readvertised... PMU not yet fully set up. (Procurement risk section)

gen_risks.description: The project’s ambitious timeline (CSC by 2017, reforms by 2020) may lead to missed milestones.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a detailed work plan with buffer periods, track milestones monthly, and apply results‑based incentives to keep teams on schedule.
gen_risks.evidence: Government’s timeline is very ambitious... compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk. (Sustainability section)

gen_risks.description: Administrative data may not capture the true time citizens spend obtaining services, compromising performance measurement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Triangulate administrative data with citizen surveys, improve data capture at service points, and conduct periodic data quality audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Administrative data does not reflect citizens’ experience... may not account for time gathering documents. (PDO Indicator description)

gen_risks.description: Operating costs of the CSC may exceed estimates, threatening fiscal sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform a detailed OPEX analysis, set a reserve fund, review costs annually, and explore PPP financing for non‑core services.
gen_risks.evidence: Operating costs for the CSC will likely be offset... ongoing operating costs include licenses and maintenance. (Financial analysis section)

gen_risks.description: Shifts in EU accession priorities could reduce political support for the reform programme.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align reform outcomes with EU standards, maintain regular dialogue with EU partners, and embed reforms in the National Strategy for Development.
gen_risks.evidence: EU progress report acknowledges political will... challenges ahead of EU accession. (EU section)

gen_risks.description: Inadequate communication may lead to low citizen awareness and trust, limiting uptake of new services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Launch a multi‑channel communication campaign, involve grassroots organisations, and monitor awareness through the citizen feedback mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: Effective communication is critical... to improve citizens’ trust and perception. (Communication section)

gen_risks.description: Delays in DLI verification and reporting could postpone RBF disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a clear verification protocol, schedule third‑party validations ahead of reporting deadlines, and train PMU staff on timely IFR preparation.
gen_risks.evidence: DLIs will be verified each calendar quarter... verification protocol provided in Annex 1. (Disbursement section)

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity poses challenges to delivering the reform effort, despite very high leadership commitment and fast-paced GoA initiation of reforms.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project Preparation Facility (PPF) is designed to assist capacity building for the implementing agency; the TA part of the loan continues building capacity to deliver, addressing the most pressing capacity needs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks related to the new form of financial instrument used in Albania.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the fiduciary risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk, named alongside the fiduciary risk as being addressed by the same TA support (fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU); not separately elaborated beyond this.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the technical design risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risks arising from inter-agency coordination.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by strong emphasis on coordination mechanisms in the design of the operation.

gt_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance to enhanced transparency and simplification of administrative processes.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated in part through high-level leadership and engagement, and through citizen feedback arrangements that help pinpoint poor performance and corruption.

gt_risks.description: Political cycle risk from elections coming up in 2017, which could disrupt reform continuity and government commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by making early progress in showing results and ensuring a broad constituency of support for the project's objectives and activities among the leadership of participating institutions and service users.
